names: Manuel José de Arriaga Brum da Silveira e Peyrelongue
summary: Manuel de Arriaga (1840–1917), a lawyer and old republican propagandist from the Azores, was elected the first president of the Portuguese Republic by the Constituent Assembly on 24 August 1911. The office the 1911 constitution gave him was weak by design — chosen by parliament, with no government of its own — but it kept the power to appoint and dismiss ministers, and in January 1915 Arriaga used it to put out the Democratic government and call General Pimenta de Castro, who then governed without the Chamber. The rising of 14 May 1915 undid that, and Arriaga resigned twelve days later. He is in the atlas as the first holder of the office through which the First Republic’s crises were settled.
